suspects.description: (int)&NAME used in arithmetic — Watcom byte-offset trampolining that should be expressed as struct field or array index access. Replace in a .keep.
(int)&NAME used in arithmetic — Watcom byte-offset trampolining that should be expressed as struct field or array index access. Replace in a .keep.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `source` self-updates via the address of a sibling field whose byte offset equals the array stride. Replace `source->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar2` self-updates via the address of a sibling field whose byte offset equals the array stride. Replace `pCVar2->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `source` self-updates by taking the address of a sibling subfield, numerically casting to `int`, then adding a small constant — the sum equals one element-size step of the array being walked. Replace `source->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar2` self-updates by taking the address of a sibling subfield, numerically casting to `int`, then adding a small constant — the sum equals one element-size step of the array being walked. Replace `pCVar2->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom inline memcpy (REP MOVSD at ????????, 4-byte stride). Ghidra reconstructs this as a countdown for-loop with element-by-element copies; replace the loop with memcpy(dst, src, count * 4) or a struct assignment in a .keep.
